prerequisites: Explanation of the constructive principles of the component elements (electrical devices, electric machines, static converters, etc.)
Adequate application of fundamental knowledge about electric machines

learning_outcomes.text: Proper implementation of specific fundamental knowledge of mathematics, physics, chemistry, in the field of electrical engineering.
Use of fundamental knowledge of electrotechnics.
Design and coordination of experiments and tests.
Acquisition of information and knowledge in the field of electric machines and their specific phenomena in terms of applications in industry.
Familiarity with practical aspects regarding the operation of electric machines through laboratory work.
Acquisition of principles and skills of design and implementation of systems containing three-phase electrical transformers through project work.

syllabus_topics: The role and place of electric machines
Field theory elements necessary in dealing with and approaching problems
Electric cars. Their constructive elements.
The single-phase electric transformer
Modes of operation of the single-phase electric transformer
The triaged electrical transformer
The modes of operation of the three-phase electric transformer
Direct current machine
Operation of direct current machines as generators
Operation of direct current machines as motors
Classification of DC motors and starting methods
Instructions on work safety techniques and methods of performing laboratory work
Single-phase transformers
Three-phase transformers
The direct current motor
The direct current generator
The universal AC motor
AC motor with capacitor
Current motor speed measurement
Reverse electromotive voltage of a DC motor
The load of a DC motor
Adjusting speed, efficiency, torque and power
Speed control of a DC motor with a closed loop
Alternator current voltage control in a closed loop
Variable cycle DC motor speed control
assessment_rules: Minimum performance standard requires: Description of the operating principles of transformers and direct current, synchronous and asynchronous electric machines. Basic knowledge of the construction and operation of electric machines. Explanation and interpretation of operating modes, phenomena that occur in the operation of electric machines, electrical and electromechanical equipment. Proper use of electrical machines and monitoring of electromechanical systems. Design of a three-phase electrical transformer of complexity. Carrying out tests for a low complexity electrical system; data analysis, measurement and interpretation.
